extracted.intended_audience: aspiring short-story writers and fiction authors seeking craft guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft guidance for composing short stories (1k–15k words) with clear structure, focused theme, and tightened cast/settings so the story is readable in one sitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count / form fit
rubrics_metrics.description: A short story is 1,000–4,000 words (can extend to 15,000); readable in one sitting. Beyond 15,000 words the demands change — the form becomes novella.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the word-count range to decide whether the work should be treated as a short story or longer fiction; prioritize readability in one sitting and the constraints that imposes on plot and character scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce characters and setting; establish the protagonist's ordinary world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a short story, exposition must be done in paragraphs, not chapters — be concise and integrate into opening scenes rather than extended backstory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rising action
rubrics_metrics.description: The inciting incident propels the story; complications mount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pressure should increase on the protagonist through escalating complications; keep momentum so the short form's arc remains taut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The pivotal moment that tests the protagonist — a decision under pressure; the story's reason for being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The climax should be the emotional/ethical test connected to the story's central concern; it must feel earned and consequential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falling action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Falling action is typically briefer than the rising action in short fiction; it should show immediate consequences and lead cleanly to resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution / Denouement
rubrics_metrics.description: The story's ending; three possible outcomes: protagonist succeeds at their stated goal; protagonist fails at their stated goal; protagonist discovers something more valuable than the goal (transformation ending).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an ending that logically follows the climax — the resolution must 'earn' the climax and connect thematically to the story's central concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme should be simple — one central concern; plot should be linear — flashbacks used sparingly; avoid complicated subplots — no room; limit character count — 3–5 named characters typical; single major setting, or at most a few.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short stories need tight focus: concentrate on one thematic question, streamline plot events, minimize named characters and settings, and avoid the narrative breadth of a novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure vs. plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot = what happens (the elements). Structure = the orderly arrangement (the timing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate structure separately from raw eventfulness — a modest plot with excellent structure can be stronger than an eventful plot with poor structure. Timing and arrangement matter in short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual reader comprehension (what & what it means)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader must understand both: what happens (events, plot) and what it means (theme, significance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure on either dimension produces a defective story — ensure clarity of events and clarity of interpretive significance without stating theme explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a known structural framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine short-story structure with a known framework (e.g., Hero's Journey, Three-Act Structure, Seven-Point Story Structure, Save the Cat) to scaffold the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frameworks not as formulaic constraints but as organizational scaffolds that help you time beats and shape meaning; choose the framework that suits the story's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: All five structural components present
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete short story contains exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing, check that each component is present and functional (not merely mentioned); in short fiction components will be compressed but must be discernible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single, focused theme
rubrics_metrics.description: The story should have one central concern rather than multiple competing themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stating theme explicitly; instead, embody the theme through character choices, plot consequences, and symbolic detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear (or motivated nonlinear) plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer a linear plot; if nonlinear techniques (flashbacks, jumps) are used, they must be clearly motivated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonlinear devices are risky in short fiction because of space constraints — only use them when they materially serve the story's theme or structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited named characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the number of named characters low — typically 3–5 named characters in a short story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fewer characters allow deeper focus on the protagonist and clearer stakes; unnamed or minor roles can be compressed or combined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax must test the protagonist meaningfully
rubrics_metrics.description: The climax should meaningfully test the protagonist in relation to the story's central concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the protagonist faces a consequential decision/pressure point tied to theme; a weak or unrelated climax undermines the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution must earn the climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The resolution/denouement should follow logically from and justify the climax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid endings that feel detached from the climax or that introduce new, unexplained elements; the ending should feel like a consequence of the protagonist's choice or failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid common short-story failures (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common failures include: trying to fit a novel's worth of plot into 4,000 words; multiple subplots; too many named characters; theme stated rather than embodied; no clear climax (story drifts); resolution that fails to connect to the climax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list as diagnostic criteria when revising: cut extraneous plotlines/characters, embody theme through action, ensure a clear, earned climax and connected resolution.
